thread:
maya: Heads-up — Seabright (Dedicated customer) is hitting p99 tail spikes during their nightly batch jobs; we're seeing request timeouts and queue growth. Logs point to a lot of cold-starts and long model load times. Anyone able to own a short-term mitigation and an owner for the triage?

sam: On it. Can you paste a sample request_id or a few log lines? Quick mitigation idea: route to a warmer reserved pool and bump min_replicas temporarily.

maya: Pasted a couple of lines from the router and pool scaler: 

```
2026-03-18T02:04:12Z router: req=8401fa pool=dedicated-seabright queue_ms=1224 cold_start=true model_load_ms=1832
2026-03-18T02:04:12Z scaler: pool=dedicated-seabright desired=6 current=2 reason=spike
2026-03-18T02:05:03Z router: req=8401fb pool=dedicated-seabright queue_ms=2100 timeout=true
```

ana: FYI — runtime kernel 2.1.7 was rolled yesterday; 2.1.7 had a change to allocator heuristics that can spike model load times under memory pressure. I have a suspected revert in 2.1.8 but need to confirm. If that's it, a rollback might help.

liam: ML infra note — the model's quantization profile causes larger on-disk artifacts that slow cold loads. I can bake a warmed image with KV cache prepopulated and push it to the pool; estimate 20-30m to produce and test.

sam: Plan proposal (short-term):
1) increase min_replicas for dedicated-seabright from 2 -> 6 for 2 hours
2) enable prefix cache on that route
3) route 30% of traffic to a canary warmed pool first, then shift more if stable
I can do the config patch + canary rollout. Rolling target in ~15m. I'll post canary rollout id here. Assigning to myself for rollout. ETA status update at 1749999100.

tara: SRE — please attach runbook and rollback steps. Also open an incident page so we have paging if things worsen. I'll stay on the bridge if needed.

deploy-bot: canary rollout started by sam at 1749998930; change id cfg-6572; target pools: dedicated-seabright-canary (3 replicas).

sam: Canary is warm and handling initial traffic; observed queue_ms dropping from ~2100 -> ~120 over 2m. Continuing to shift to canary.

maya: Thanks. Owners: sam = routing + rollout, liam = warmed model image + validation, ana = runtime kernel triage. Tara = SRE/runbook + escalation path. Please post timestamps for completion updates. Next checkpoint at 1749999100. If SLA impact >5% before then, escalate immediately.

liam: Starting build of warmed image now; will push artifact tag `seabright-warm-20260318` and notify when uploaded (~25m).

ana: I'm reproducing the allocator regression on staging now; if confirmed I'll prepare a 2.1.8 rollback candidate and coordinate with sam for a safe rollout window.

sam: Will keep traffic on canary until liam's warm image is verified. If runtime rollback looks safe, we can do that as a second mitigation.

maya: Appreciate the quick commits. Short notes to include in the customer update: 1) temporary capacity bump + canary in progress, 2) model warm image build underway, 3) runtime kernel being investigated. I'll draft and send to CS once we have liam's artifact or a kernel decision.

tara: Runbook link: https://wiki.redwood/seabright-dedicated-runbook — added rollback steps and paging contact.

sam: Canary to stable shift started at 1749999025; increasing pool min_replicas to 6 for next 2 hours (change id cfg-6573).

maya: Update noted. Please post final resolution here when stable so I can close the customer loop.

sam: Update 1749999120 — traffic stable, p99 down to pre-incident numbers. Leaving min_replicas=4 for another hour then scaling to normal.

maya: Closing loop: owners did the mitigations; liam to provide warm-image details and ana to confirm kernel RCA. I'll follow up with CS to confirm SLA exposure. Thanks everyone.
